text:
ashley: Heads-up — Acme Manufacturing asked whether we can run a 4-week on‑prem POC in a locked production plant. Constraints: no persistent egress (one outbound window per week allowed), hardware HSM (YubiHSM2), strict telemetry opt‑out, and they only accept quarterly patch windows. They want: feasibility, upgrade/patch plan, offline activation flow, and rough pricing for Dedicated vs Private. Can we confirm what’s possible?
ben: Thanks — couple clarifying q's: do they want Redwood Private (full control plane on their network) or Dedicated (reserved infra in our cloud with controlled egress)? Also need exact HSM model/driver details and whether they can accept a jumpbox for the weekly egress window.
ashley: They prefer Private but will consider Dedicated if offline activation is allowed. HSM model: YubiHSM2 (vendor lib, no internet), kernel is locked down (no new kernel modules). Jumpbox allowed once/week to pull bundles.
ravi: @ashley @ben quick notes from runtime side: we support customer‑managed key stores via PKCS#11 and KMS integrations normally. YubiHSM2 is not in our standard test matrix but it exposes an API we can integrate with. Constraints:
- If kernel modules are blocked we need a userland daemon that talks to the HSM (YubiHSM2 offers a client lib).
- Offline activation is doable: we can generate a signed offline license manifest and a delta bundle you pull during the weekly window.
- Patch cadence: we can package quarterly cumulative updates + emergency hotfixes as signed binaries. Hotfixes require pre‑signed approval flow (customer signs acceptance).
camille: Security checklist items I care about (for the questionnaire):
- telemetry: can be fully disabled at build/runtime for Private installs — we provide an opt‑out flag and a signed attestation that no telemetry was sent from nodes.
- data‑at‑rest: full disk + model artifact encryption supported; we rely on a customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping.
- SBOM & provenance: we can ship signed SBOMs and commit hashes for model bundles.
- FIPS requirement? If they insist we have a FIPS‑validated build path but we need to know which components must be FIPS.
ashley: Good — they asked specifically about "offline license keys" and whether we can do USB/disk shipping of updates. Also they asked whether we can sign bundles with their HSM.
ravi: USB/sneakernet is fine. Two implementation patterns:
1) Customer signs bundles with the YubiHSM private key (preferred for max control). We provide signing templates and verification built into the agent.
2) Redwood signs bundles and we provide a signed manifest; customer validates signature with our public key.
For (1) we need the HSM client lib on the node (userland) and an operator flow for offline signing (we can supply a small signing helper). Example helper (concept):
```
# generate activation manifest
rdwctl offline-generate --instance acme-poc --timestamp 2026-04-01 > manifest.json
# sign with local HSM (user runs this inside airgapped room)
hsm-sign --lib /usr/lib/libyubihsm.so --key-label rdw-sign manifest.json > manifest.sig
# place manifest+sig alongside bundle for pull
```
ben: For pricing conversation: high level — Dedicated (reserved pools) is usage-based with monthly commit; Private has a platform/license fee + installation + optional support tiers. For an air‑gapped POC we usually quote a one‑time Private onboarding fee (engineering + ops) plus a small recurring license. I'll pull a template SOW.
ashley: They want an acceptance criteria list for the POC: model latency within X, offline upgrade apply in <1 hour, and no outbound telemetry. We should avoid hard numbers until perf run.
ops-bot: Created ticket RDW-8132: "Acme airgap POC — HSM integration & offline activation" assigned to @ravi. Link: https://redwood.example/tickets/RDW-8132
ravi: Next steps from eng:
- I’ll spin up an isolated test with YubiHSM2 in our lab (driver in userland) and validate signing/verify flow.
- Prepare a signed bundle + manifest example for their ops to exercise during weekly pull.
- Estimate delta size: depends on quantized model artifacts; expect 200MB–4GB typical.
camille: I can start filling the security questionnaire sections we control (telemetry, SBOM, encryption, incident contact). Please DM me the customer questionnaire PDF.
ashley: I'll schedule a 30m tech presales call with Acme + eng + security for tomorrow 10am PT. Ben — can you draft the SOW template and a high‑level cost outline? Ravi/Camille — plz bring the checklist and a short demo plan.
ben: Will do, dropping a skeleton SOW in the ticket by EOD. :+1:
ravi: I'll post the lab validation notes and the sample manifest in the ticket.
camille: I’ll attach the partial SQ answers and the FIPS questions to the ticket.
ashley: Thanks team — I'll update the customer. :rocket:
